method: For each (image, class), each radiologist's boxes were scored as predictions against the other radiologists' boxes as ground truth, at IoU thresholds 0.50:0.95:0.05, averaged across thresholds. This is a precision-style measure of inter-annotator localisation consistency, not a true mAP — it omits recall and confidence ranking, so it bounds achievable agreement rather than reproducing the model metric exactly.
observations: Model exceeds the human ceiling on Cardiomegaly (109%) and Aortic enlargement (112%), consistent with having learned WBF-merged consensus targets — it predicts the average of three radiologists, which agrees with any individual better than two individuals agree with each other.
The ceiling is low across most classes (Pleural thickening 0.163, Other lesion 0.238), indicating limited achievable performance rather than model failure.
Calcification (11.8% of ceiling) and Other lesion (12.2%) show the largest unrealised headroom.
Pneumothorax is the clearest candidate for a data-volume constraint: ceiling 0.585 (second highest) but only 25.6% realised, on 96 training images.
